name: Nerite USND
oneLiner: USND was Nerite's Liquity-v2 fork CDP dollar on Arbitrum; supply collapsed after the rsETH hack impaired an approved collateral branch.

blacklistabilityReview.sourceFreeRationale: Resolved from Pharos stablecoin metadata by the blacklistability resolver as no identified direct, upstream, or possible freeze exposure; no separate manual override source is attached.
blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Inferred review retained: USND resolves to No because existing metadata does not identify direct, upstream, or possible freeze exposure.

obituary.obituary: Nerite built USND on immutable Liquity V2-style contracts, but one of its approved collateral branches depended on rsETH. After the rsETH hack impaired that collateral, Nerite could not simply patch the market away or rewrite the risk controls. Supply collapsed from a $2.7M peak to under $100K, leaving USND as an archived case study in how immutable CDP systems can still inherit external collateral failure when a supported asset breaks upstream.

collateral: tBTC, WETH, wstETH, rETH, rsETH, weETH, ARB, and COMP in immutable overcollateralized CDP markets on Arbitrum
pegMechanism: Overcollateralized CDP with user-set interest rates and direct on-chain redemption for underlying collateral; separate Stability Pools absorb liquidations per collateral market

mintAuthority.summary: USND was a Liquity-v2 friendly fork on Arbitrum: USND is minted only when users open Troves and borrow against approved collateral branches through immutable, governance-minimized BorrowerOperations contracts. The core code can never be upgraded and there is no privileged admin able to mint USND directly.

controls.label: Nerite BorrowerOperations / CollateralRegistry (immutable Liquity-v2 fork)
controls.evidence: Nerite is a Liquity-v2 fork with immutable, governance-minimized contracts; USND mints only via per-branch BorrowerOperations against user collateral, with a single BoldToken and CollateralRegistry, and no upgrade path or admin mint.

review.evidence: Nerite docs and the NeriteOrg/nerite Liquity-v2 monorepo fork describe immutable, non-upgradeable core contracts where USND is minted only through user Troves/BorrowerOperations; mechanism matches Liquity v2's renounced-admin design, though live owner() renouncement was not independently read on-chain.
review.sourceFreeRationale: Immutability/no-admin-mint established from project docs and the Liquity-v2 fork lineage; the on-chain owner()/renouncement state was not independently read, hence manual-review rather than verified.
unresolvedQuestions: Confirm on-chain that no system contract retains an owner/admin able to mint or alter collateral branches.
Phase 0c (2026-06-11): immutable/no-privileged-mint classification still needs a fresh source-code or native-chain specialist confirmation before verified confidence.
